title: Pressure Washing Pricing: What to Charge
description: Pressure washing prices to charge in 2026 by surface and square foot, with minimum charges, a worked job, and a pricing checklist.

cover.alt: Illustration of a pressure washer wand on a for pros blueprint background with a measuring tape

keywords: how much to charge for pressure washing
pressure washing cost per square foot
takeaways: HomeGuide lists pressure washing at $0.08 to $0.20 per square foot for cold water work, with most jobs at $173 to $311 total.
Price by surface, not one flat rate. Driveways, siding, decks, and roofs take different time, pressure, and risk.
Set a minimum charge and hold it. Small jobs still cost a trip, setup, and cleanup.
body:
Charge for pressure washing by surface and square foot, with a minimum charge on every job. HomeGuide 2026 data puts cold water pressure washing at $0.08 to $0.20 per square foot, most homeowner jobs at $173 to $311 total, and driveways at $100 to $260 each. If your quote sits far below those figures, you are likely paying for the job yourself in fuel, time, and wear.

## 2026 prices by surface to price against

One rate for every surface is the fastest way to lose money in this trade. Flat concrete is fast. Siding needs care, decks need a gentle touch, and roofs add risk and time.

| Surface | Typical price | Rate note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Driveway | $100 to $260 | $0.25 to $0.35 per sq ft for a standard wash |
| House and siding | $170 to $360 | About $265 average for a house wash |
| Deck or patio | $200 to $240 | About $0.35 per sq ft for a deck |
| Fence, 100 ft by 6 ft | $180 to $300 | $0.30 to $0.50 per sq ft of fence face |
| Roof | $250 to $600 | $0.15 to $0.70 per sq ft, method matters |

All ranges in the table are from HomeGuide pressure washing prices for 2026. The same source lists hot water power washing higher, at $0.35 to $0.77 per square foot, because hot water gear costs more to buy and run and cuts grease faster. Charge more for hot water work. Do not give it away at cold water rates.

Angi puts patios at $0.10 to $0.50 per square foot, concrete at $130 to $220, brick or paver at $210 to $250. HomeGuide pro bands are wider: driveway $0.10 to $0.40, exterior $0.15 to $0.50, deck $0.30 to $0.80, roof $0.40 to $1.00. Use the low end for big open work, the high end for tight or stained work.

## The pricing formula and your minimum charge

**Job price = (Surface 1 sq ft x Rate 1) + (Surface 2 sq ft x Rate 2) + Add-ons**

**Final quote = Job price, or your minimum charge, whichever is higher**

Pick a minimum and print it on your quote sheet. HomeGuide notes many firms set a minimum in the $75 to $150 range in related cost data, and its main price page lists a $100 minimum cost for pro work. For a solo operator with a truck, trailer, and insurance, $125 to $150 is a sane floor in most towns. A 15 minute walkway wash still costs a drive, unload, hookup, wash, rinse, reload, and drive back. That is an hour of your day, priced or not.

Measure the surface, not the house, for flatwork. A driveway that is 20 ft wide and 30 ft long is 600 sq ft, no matter what size home sits behind it. For siding, many firms price by the square foot of wall or by the linear foot of house: HomeGuide lists about $1 per linear foot for one story and $2 per linear foot for two stories. State on the quote which method you used, so there is no argument later.

If you wash before paint work, price the wash as its own line. Our [painting estimate calculator](/blog/painting-estimate-calculator/) helps you keep prep and paint as separate, clear lines.

## Worked example: driveway plus patio in one visit

A client wants a concrete driveway and a concrete patio washed in one visit.

Measurements: driveway 20 ft x 30 ft = 600 sq ft. Patio 15 ft x 20 ft = 300 sq ft. Total flatwork: 600 + 300 = 900 sq ft.

Rates: driveway at $0.30 per sq ft, inside the HomeGuide driveway band. Patio at $0.40 per sq ft, above driveway rate because of furniture moving and edging care, and inside the Angi patio band of $0.10 to $0.50.

Step 1, driveway price. 600 x $0.30 = $180.00.

Step 2, patio price. 300 x $0.40 = $120.00.

Step 3, job price. $180.00 + $120.00 = $300.00.

Step 4, minimum check. $300.00 is above a $150 minimum, so the quote stays $300.00.

Check the math a second way. Weighted average rate: $300.00 / 900 sq ft = $0.33 per sq ft. That sits inside both surface bands and near the HomeGuide average of $0.40 per sq ft for pro work. Check each part against the market table: driveway $180 sits inside $100 to $260, patio $120 sits just below the $200 to $240 deck and patio average because this patio is plain concrete with no stain work. The quote is fair and you can explain every line.

Add-ons, priced apart: oil stain treatment, algae pre-treat, or sealing. Bundling both surfaces into one visit saved the client a second trip charge, so say so on the quote.

## Pricing checklist you can use today

Use this before you send any quote.

- Each surface listed apart, with its own square feet and rate
- Water access at the home confirmed, and hose length needed noted
- Stains named: oil, rust, algae, or paint, with a treatment price if needed
- Method named: pressure wash, soft wash, or hot water power wash
- Plants, outlets, and doors to protect, noted on the quote
- Minimum charge applied, and shown if it set the price
- Travel beyond your normal area priced in, not added as a surprise
- Before and after photos promised, which help you sell the next job on the street

Soft wash work needs its own rate. Roofs, vinyl, painted wood, and stucco can be damaged by high pressure. Chemical cost, dwell time, and plant care are higher, so price it above flatwork. Roof work and second story siding also add ladder risk. HomeGuide lists roof washing at $250 to $600. If a job needs a second person for safety, that labor goes in the price.

## What moves a pressure washing price up or down?

Up: oil and rust stains, heavy algae, second stories, roofs, long hose runs, no water access on site, tight gates, and furniture or planters to move and replace. Commercial work after hours also prices higher.

Down: large open flatwork, several surfaces in one visit, neighbors booked on the same day, and repeat work on a set route. A 1,200 sq ft driveway at a lower per foot rate can pay better per hour than three small jobs at a higher rate, because you set up once.

Watch the per hour check. HomeGuide lists pro rates at $50 to $160 per hour. If your $300 job takes 2.5 hours with travel and setup, that is $120 per hour gross. If you need $130, nudge rates up $0.03 to $0.05 per sq ft on the next quote. Do not race to the bottom. Hold a minimum, show photos, and use a clear line by line quote like our [free estimate template](/blog/free-estimate-template/).

## Frequently asked questions

### How much should I charge to pressure wash a driveway?
For a standard two car driveway of about 600 sq ft, $150 to $210 is a fair 2026 range at $0.25 to $0.35 per sq ft. HomeGuide average for a driveway is $100 to $260 total. Heavy oil stains or a long, steep drive push you to the top of the range.

### What is a good minimum charge for pressure washing?
Set $125 to $150 if you run insured with your own gear and trailer. Small jobs under your minimum still get quoted, at the minimum. Customers accept a clear minimum far more often than owners fear, as long as you state it up front.

### Should I charge by the hour or by the square foot?
By the square foot, by surface, for almost all home work. It is easy for the client to check and it pays you for speed as you improve. Keep an hourly check for yourself after each job to spot work types that pay badly.

### How much more should soft washing cost?
Price soft washing above standard flatwork rates for the same area. Chemical cost, dwell time, plant care, and damage risk are all higher. Many firms price house soft washes in the same $170 to $360 house range HomeGuide lists, with larger or two story homes at the top.

### Do I need insurance to charge pro prices?
Yes. Clients paying market rates expect a licensed and insured firm, and one siding or window claim wipes out a season of profit. HomeGuide makes the same point to homeowners when it warns that a very low bid can signal a lack of experience or cover.

### How do I price a whole house wash?
Measure or estimate the wall area or use linear feet of the home: about $1 per linear foot for one story and $2 for two stories, per HomeGuide. Then check the result against the $170 to $360 house range. A very large or three story home will sit above that range, and the quote should say why.
